title: Tina S NDE 710
content:
7356 In the basement of our house, I was helping my husband with locksmithing job. I moved his gun, in its holster, to work on the locks. As I was beginning to set the weapon on the floor, it slipped out of the holster and rotated. It was pointing toward me and fell hammer first onto a metal stand. The Ruger Blackhawk .357 revolver had a defective safety and fired. I saw, heard, felt, and smelled the gun/bullet in that order. I grabbed my abdomen. The bullet had entered left and about 3 inches from my navel. The only pain at that time was a burning sensation at the entrance sight. I screamed for my husband, who was outside, and walked to the open door. When he saw my wound (he was a retired firefighter/emergency medical technician), he grabbed me and laid me on the floor. We lived in the country, so I was taken by ambulance to a school where the helicopter met us and flew me to the medical center. During the flight I was conscious the entire time. As we landed at the hospital, the paramedic radioed that my BP was 50/0. The surgical team met us at the landing pad and I was taken right into surgery. They put a mask over my face and I convulsed as they gave me a paralyzing drug. As they intubated me, I heard a nurse say 'Okay, she's ready.' I felt a searing/cutting from the top of my sternum down my torso. I could only scream in my mind that I was still conscious and wasn't asleep. I felt the surgeon lift up the right side of my intestines and then the left side looking for damage. On a pain scale of 1 to 10, that was a 15. I was pleading for God to take me, it was so excruciating. When the doctor stopped, I said 'never mind.' He then worked higher in my torso; I felt sewing around my right lung. I then became aware of a light off to my left. I no longer felt my body, but I believe I was still in it. I realized that my grandmother and great-grandmother were standing at the entrance to the light. My grandmother had died in 1978 and I had never met my great-grandmother. Both were native. They told me by telepathy, that it was not my time and that I had more to do. During this time, I have no idea how long this lasted. I was completely immersed in the most incredible love, contentment, acceptance, feeling of being home, that you only could imagine. In fact, we don't have words to describe the feelings. The next memory I have is my internist asking me to squeeze his hand. When I had my NDE, the surgeon was giving me heart massage to keep me alive. No one expected me to live. The recovery was awful, but I did it. The surgeon was horrified that I was awake for the surgery. They compared my memories with the recording and I was right.

boundary_and_return.mission_detail: Told by grandmother and great-grandmother (telepathically) that it was not her time and that she had more to do.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Accidental gunshot wound from a Ruger Blackhawk .357 revolver with a defective safety.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Experience occurred while patient reports being conscious during surgery and in extreme pain; later surgeon compared memories with recording and 'I was right.'
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: No OBE or tunnel reported; light appeared during surgery, with deceased relatives at the entrance to the light; then return to awareness in hospital.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: NDE elements occurred while she reports remaining in her body during surgery and being awake/paralyzed; later says the surgeon was giving heart massage during the NDE; memories were compared with a recording and she reports they were accurate.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: 'Okay, she's ready.'; 'I was completely immersed in the most incredible love, contentment, acceptance, feeling of being home...'; 'we don't have words to describe the feelings.'; 'it was not my time and that I had more to do.'
